article.title: NFL EDGE Wednesday Evening Brief
article.dek: The Week 3 card changed shape tonight: the Giants and Colts are in, Seattle and Las Vegas are out, and Minnesota got slightly more expensive.

items.headline: The Giants change quarterbacks, and Indianapolis loses a starting receiver
paragraphs: The biggest update is in New York. Jaxson Dart is expected to undergo season-ending knee surgery, and Jameis Winston will start Sunday against Tennessee. The Giants also had Malik Nabers limited Wednesday, while left tackle Andrew Thomas missed practice but still has a chance to return.

Indianapolis is putting Alec Pierce on injured reserve after he aggravated his heel injury. Across the rest of the slate, Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold returned to practice on a limited basis with his glute injury, Baltimore receiver Zay Flowers missed Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury, and Puka Nacua did not practice for the Rams because of his hip.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Two of tonight's card changes land directly on the injury news
paragraphs: The Giants are now an NFL EDGE moneyline play at DraftKings -148, playable through -150, with Winston taking over for Dart. That quarterback change is real context, but it is already known information; it is not a reason to pay past the Play Through.

Indianapolis also returned to the card at +2.5 (-104), playable through -107, on the same day Pierce moved to injured reserve. The recommendation already exists with that news in the market. Treat the current number as the decision point rather than trying to outguess the injury headline.

items.headline: Indianapolis has the useful disagreement tonight
paragraphs: This is a broad public-betting/line-movement signal, not a DraftKings-vs-Circa split. Action Network currently shows 58% of spread bets on Indianapolis, yet its board has moved from Colts +1.5 at open to +2.5. In plain English: more tickets are on Indianapolis, but the market has still given Colts bettors an extra point.

That disagreement is worth noticing because NFL EDGE also has Indianapolis +2.5. It is not proof that the Colts are wrong or that the other side is smarter; it simply means the price movement is not following the majority of tickets.
items.takeaway: Stay disciplined rather than automatically fading Indianapolis. The verified NFL EDGE play is Colts +2.5 (-104) at DraftKings, playable through -107. Take the recommendation only inside that limit; if the price gets worse, do not chase it.

items.headline: Giants and Colts arrive as Seattle and Las Vegas roll off
paragraphs: The newest NFL EDGE card replaces Seattle moneyline with the Giants moneyline at DraftKings -148, playable through -150 for 1.0u. Indianapolis +2.5 returns at DraftKings -104, playable through -107 for 1.0u, replacing Las Vegas +3.
Minnesota moneyline stays on the card but got a little more expensive: DraftKings moved from -120 to -122, and the Play Through moved from -123 to -125. The recommended stake remains 0.75u.
items.takeaway: This is a real card reshuffle, not a cosmetic price refresh. Use the Giants, Colts and Minnesota terms shown now; the old Seattle and Las Vegas recommendations are no longer current plays.

items.headline: A returning play gets a fresh price limit
paragraphs: Indianapolis was on the opening Week 3 card, disappeared, and is back tonight. Do not revive the old ticket terms from memory. When a recommendation returns, use the book, price and Play Through attached to the new appearance; the old version is history.

sources.label: NFL EDGE canonical Week 3 prospective evidence

evidence.fact: NFL.com's Wednesday roundup reports that Jaxson Dart is expected to undergo season-ending knee surgery and Jameis Winston will start for the Giants against Tennessee; Malik Nabers was limited and Andrew Thomas did not practice but has a chance to return. Indianapolis will place Alec Pierce on injured reserve with a heel injury. Sam Darnold was limited in his return to Seattle practice, Zay Flowers did not practice for Baltimore with a hamstring injury, and Puka Nacua did not practice for the Rams with a hip injury.

The dedicated VSiN DraftKings and Circa NFL split pages were deliberately checked first, but their accessible rendered tables did not expose reliable game-specific rows for the NFL EDGE plays. Action Network was therefore used as the backup public-betting source. Its current board shows Indianapolis receiving 58% of spread bets while the listed spread moved from Colts +1.5 at open to +2.5, an opposite-direction public-betting/line-movement signal. The article explicitly labels this as broad public betting plus line movement, not a DraftKings-vs-Circa split, and does not characterize it as sharp money.

Kickoff-window weather was checked for the relevant outdoor Giants-Titans and Vikings-Buccaneers games. Available forecasts did not establish a sufficiently material weather issue for the reader-facing brief: Tampa was forecast hot but with light wind and low precipitation risk, while MetLife forecasts varied on wind and precipitation. No weather claim was included in the article.

The production NFL EDGE app was attempted as a cross-check but was not accessible through the available web reader during this run. Canonical prospective-card evidence remained authoritative for Market Watch.
